verdict.headline: Asia chip rout and China DUV breakthrough deepen semiconductor distress as FOMC Day 1 begins
verdict.label: Step Aside — KOSPI -10.8%, SK Hynix -14.7%, Samsung -13.4%; China begins mass-producing domestic DUV lithography machines (ASML -8.4%); NVDA circular financing unresolved; NQ futures -0.9%; BTC $63,429 ($1,429 above Gate 2 at $62,000); tomorrow's FOMC decision + META/MSFT AH is the only clearing event
verdict.rationale_short: Tuesday pre-market read-in: The chip sector is in acute distress. South Korea's KOSPI collapsed 10.8% — its worst single-session decline in nearly a decade — as Samsung Electronics sank 13.4% and SK Hynix tumbled 14.7%, both dragged down by the compounding narratives of Nvidia's $250B OpenAI circular financing deal (confirmed WSJ/Bloomberg Monday) and a new development: The Information reported Monday that China has begun mass production of domestically developed immersion DUV lithography machines, directly threatening ASML's export-controlled equipment monopoly in the Chinese market. ASML fell 8.4% in Amsterdam, with AEX -0.82%, BE Semiconductor -9.7%, and ASM International -7.1%. The selloff has spread to US premarket: Nvidia -1.2% (extending Monday's -5%), AMD -3%, Micron -5%, Nikkei -4.3%, Taiwan -4%. S&P 500 futures are down only 0.1% as Dow futures +0.3% indicate rotation into defensives — the divergence is real but does not offset the sectoral carnage. Oil has extended its decline: Brent is at $85.08 (-3.71%), approaching the $85 formal regime clearance trigger for the first time since the Iran conflict began; WTI is at $80.11 (-3%) as Trump said the US is holding 'good talks' with Iran. The oil improvement is the one constructive signal — but it arrives amid a deepening multi-front semiconductor crisis that is distinctly not oil-driven. BTC fell to $63,429 (-2.85%) per live Crypto.com data, $1,429 above Gate 2 ($62,000); multi-asset risk-off is spreading. FOMC meeting Day 1 begins today (decision tomorrow July 29 2pm ET, Warsh press conference 2:30pm); September hike probability remains elevated (~70-82%). META and MSFT report AH tomorrow — the week's clearing event has not arrived. The call: step aside. Do not add chip exposure ahead of a fully unresolved dual-catalyst sequence (FOMC + Mag-7 earnings) with the semiconductor sector in free fall.

KOSPI -10.8%, SK Hynix -14.7%, Samsung -13.4% represents institutional reassessment of AI memory demand reliability — the HBM demand thesis is structurally linked to NVDA data center orders, which are now under circular financing scrutiny. SMH tracks the sector; August puts capture the NVDA earnings binary.
trade_setups.entry: Buy SMH August puts at the open; strike near current level (~$230-235 area if tracking the Asia selloff direction). Target SMH -8-12% if FOMC hawkish hold AND MSFT/META capex disappoints. Stop: SMH recovers above Tuesday open price within 48 hours of FOMC statement.

trade_setups.horizon: Through NVDA Q2 FY27 August 26; primary inflection point at FOMC July 29 + MSFT/META AH

trade_setups.thesis: Wednesday's FOMC statement is the year's highest-information event. With September hike probability still ~70-75% and Brent approaching but not yet clearing the $85 trigger, Warsh faces a genuinely ambiguous input set. If he acknowledges September as live (Brent still above $85, 30Y at 5.10%), TBT long profits. If he explicitly closes September (Brent nearly at clearance, oil path down), TLT rallies. The pair captures the binary without betting on direction; FOMC ends the ambiguity in 30 minutes.

trade_setups.horizon: Through FOMC July 29; convert survivor leg to 2-3 week hold through August CPI (est. Aug 13)

bear_case: Counter-argument: The Asia chip rout is being misread as a new catalyst when it is merely the same Monday catalysts re-pricing across time zones with leverage. South Korean pension and retail investors are proportionally more exposed to SK Hynix and Samsung than US institutions are to NVDA; the -10.8% KOSPI move reflects domestic positioning, not a fresh information update. The China DUV lithography story has significant caveats: production is initially five machines in 2026 and twenty in 2027, the technology lags ASML's latest immersion systems in throughput and overlay precision, and yield quality at volume remains unproven. ASML's core EUV moat — which covers leading-edge AI accelerator chip production — is entirely untouched. The constructive case: Brent at $85.08 is sitting directly at the $85 formal regime clearance trigger; a single session of Iran diplomatic progress could push Brent below $85 and begin clearing the regime breach count for the first time since the conflict began. September hike probability would reprice meaningfully below 70% (the formal trigger) if oil clears and FOMC language is dovish. If SPX holds 7,380 through today's session and FOMC tomorrow is a dovish hold, the entire Asia chip narrative becomes a buying opportunity in AAPL, AVGO, and broad quality tech. Bear case invalidation: Brent closes below $85 today AND FOMC explicitly closes September tomorrow AND MSFT/META both clear the GOOGL AI capex template. If all three occur simultaneously, the step-aside call is wrong. If SPX reclaims 7,480 on the close of July 29 post-FOMC, the call is wrong.
